Group indices by value; within a sorted group of positions L, the sum for position p splits into left contributions p*L[p] - prefix(L[0..p-1]) and right contributions suffix(L[p+1..]) - (k-1-p)*L[p]. Example 1: value 3 sits at indices 2,5,6; for index 2 the sum is 3+4=7. Brute force is O(n^2) — too slow for n = 1e5, so grouping with prefix sums (or an equivalent two-pass running sum) is required.

Sum of |x - a_i| over sorted positions = (left count * x - left sum) + (right sum - right count * x).

Per group, compute prefix sums of positions.
For the p-th member at position x: answer = x*p - pre[p] + (pre[k]-pre[p+1]) - x*(k-1-p).
a.t: O(n) — bucketing plus one linear pass per group
a.sp: O(n) for the groups and prefix arrays

s: Forward pass: res[i] += cnt[x]*i - sum[x], then increment cnt[x] and add i to sum[x].
Backward pass: res[i] += sum[x] - cnt[x]*i, then update the trackers.

c.python:
from collections import defaultdict
class Solution:
    def getDistances(self, arr):
        n = len(arr)
        res = [0] * n
        cnt, s = defaultdict(int), defaultdict(int)
        for i, x in enumerate(arr):
            res[i] += cnt[x] * i - s[x]
            cnt[x] += 1
            s[x] += i
        cnt, s = defaultdict(int), defaultdict(int)
        for i in range(n - 1, -1, -1):
            x = arr[i]
            res[i] += s[x] - cnt[x] * i
            cnt[x] += 1
            s[x] += i
        return res

a.t: O(n) — two linear passes with O(1) hash work each

w: Use 64-bit sums: with n = 1e5 identical values the total can reach ~5e14. The two-pass version avoids building explicit groups and is slightly more cache-friendly. Pitfall: forgetting the second (backward) pass, which yields only left-side distances. Follow-up: adapt to circular distance on a ring.
